### 1. What the caller expresses, and how the simulator behaves

Ntando Mkhwebane states object, timing, boundary and authorisation:

- **Object**: "the Seattle one, two rooms, four nights, checking out today, and the confirmation is
  PH36DTL9."
- **Result asked for**: "he is leaving today, he would like the stay closed off properly and the
  balance taken off the card on file, and he would like to be told what that figure is before he
  gets in the car."
- **Timing**: "This is not a query for later — he wants it done now."
- **Authorisation**: "He is happy for the desk to sort out whatever it needs to sort out on his
  behalf … anything the desk cannot do for him he will do himself, there and then." Conditionally:
  "If the desk explains that something has to go onto the bill before the balance can be struck he
  simply says that is fine, go ahead. If the desk explains that the property credit on the booking
  has to be spent by him rather than applied for him, he laughs and says pass it over, and he runs
  it when the agent hands it to him."

Passive throughout: mobile `7020863419`, passport last four `2907`, declines to guess the email
("he cannot remember which email he used to book and says so rather than guessing"), answers party
composition when asked ("five adults across the two rooms — one of his colleagues brought his
brother at the last minute — and no children"), confirms a minibar bill exists without a figure ("he
has no idea what it comes to"), names the deposit currency ("Canadian dollars"). He names no tool, no
policy and no order of work, and "does not know the figure in advance and will not guess at one."

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

The caller asks for **one** thing: close the stay and take the balance. The tree has four problems.

```
P4  the balance settled at departure                (root — what he asked for)          4th
 ├── P2  the statutory tax due on the room money for the stay                            3rd
 │     └── P1  the supplement for occupants beyond standard occupancy                     1st
 └── P3  the property credit drawn down against the charges it may be spent against       2nd (any time before P4)
```

**Hop P4 → P2 — marked `state-derived`.**

1. The root's own document, `closing_off_a_stay_at_departure_dfdbccc2`, under "What governs the
   balance":
   > **"The balance settled at departure is struck only once the folio carries the statutory tax due
   > on the room money for the stay."** *"While either of those lines is absent from the
   > reservation's folio, the balance settled at departure is not struck."*

   A record-visible state, with the ordering connective "only once". No tool, no policy, no route.
2. The folio query returns 16 rows whose `charge_category` values are `deposit`, `room_night`,
   `resort_fee`, `resort_credit_grant` and `incidental_minibar`. **No statutory tax line stands.**
3. Searching the corpus with the state's own words — "statutory tax", "room money for the stay" —
   finds `levying_statutory_tax_on_a_hotel_stay_84ffc524`, whose own rule describes the write in the
   same vocabulary: *"that tax is charged to the reservation and shown on its folio as a tax line …
   Once the charge is recorded, the tax joins what the guest owes for the stay and stands on the
   folio as a tax line."* Its amount is governed by
   `statutory_tax_due_on_a_stay_cae4b4ec`, reached from the same words.

**Hop P2 → P1 — marked `state-derived`.**

1. P2's own document, `levying_statutory_tax_on_a_hotel_stay_84ffc524`:
   > **"The statutory tax due is settled only once the folio's room lines carry every occupant
   > beyond the rate plan's standard occupancy for the nights of the stay already posted."**
   > *"While the folio's room lines fall short of carrying every such occupant for those nights, the
   > statutory tax due is not settled."*
2. Checking it against the records: the standard occupancy of a Member Flex room is 2 adults
   (`standard_occupancy_on_breakfast_plans_9f6b5fac`, the prepayment lines covering 2 rooms), so
   2 × 2 = 4 across the rooms held, against `adults_count: 5` — one occupant stands beyond. The
   folio's charge rows reach `guest_sequence` 2 and carry no line charging for that occupant. The
   state does not hold.
3. Searching with the state's words — "occupants beyond the standard occupancy", "sharing the
   rooms" — finds `charging_for_occupants_sharing_a_room_11c166f5`, which describes the write:
   *"a supplement for those occupants is charged to the reservation … Once it is recorded, the
   supplement shows on the folio alongside the room nights."* Its amount is governed by
   `supplement_for_occupants_beyond_standard_occupancy_44c948cd`.

**Hop P4 → P3 — marked `state-derived`.**

1. The root's own document, second sentence of the same block:
   > **"The balance settled at departure is struck only once the folio carries the property credit
   > drawn down against the charges it may be spent against."**
2. The folio carries two `resort_credit_grant` rows but **no drawdown row**; `resort_credit_balance_usd`
   still stands at the full 100.0. The state does not hold.
3. Searching with the state's own words — "property credit", "drawn down", "charges it may be spent
   against" — finds `spending_property_credit_during_a_stay_c04451d8`: *"One call posts a drawdown
   line to the reservation's folio for the amount stated, carrying it as value leaving the credit."*
   Its amount is governed by `property_credit_drawn_down_on_a_stay_e2f71324`. That document also
   tells me the write is the guest's own: *"This is the guest's own tool over their own reservation.
   It is unlocked and then handed over to be run by the customer themselves"* — which the persona
   answers to ("pass it over, and he runs it when the agent hands it to him").

P1 and P3 carry no prerequisite sentence of their own; I read every stay document and no further
"only once / only after / not … until" sentence governs either. The tree stops at four.

**No hop was pre-solved.** `closing_off_a_stay_at_departure_dfdbccc2` names only its own tool,
`settle_departure_balance_f8243430`, in its own invocation block; it never names
`post_statutory_tax_charge_0b7e8f18`, `spend_resort_credit_ff384f87` or
`post_occupancy_supplement_f6d09258`, never says which to run first, and carries no dependency table,
checklist or ordered route. Likewise `levying_statutory_tax_on_a_hotel_stay_84ffc524` names only
`post_statutory_tax_charge_0b7e8f18`. Each hop cost a read of the state, a folio query and a search
on the state's own vocabulary.

Verified verbatim in all six documents that name the quantity. |

Both alternatives happen to give 3 here in any case for the fee rows. |

| Markup taken from a different plan's row | Member Flex Rate carries 2.5 % in both agency_service_fee_and_conversion_tariff_863e3a65 and conversion_markup_on_a_departure_balance_08018af7. |

**One boundary re-checked as the brief asked.** The facility-fee sentence
*"The property facility fee posted on the reservation is charged in full, being owed per room per
night on every plan that does not waive it."* I read it as single-reading and take the 174.00 posted.
The competing participial reading — treating the adjunct as an instruction to recompute the fee at
the plan's 29.0 per room per night over 2 rooms and all 4 nights, 232.00 — is excluded, on the
corpus alone, by three things:

1. The subject is *"The property facility fee **posted on the reservation**"*, a restrictive
   postmodifier fixing the quantity to what stands on the folio; *"charged in full"* then fixes the
   share at the whole of that quantity, with no other base named.
2. The same noun phrase is used elsewhere in the corpus for a folio-read quantity and nowhere for a
   tariff-recomputed one: *"The facility element is the property facility fee posted on the
   reservation"* (money_returned_on_a_cancellation_settlement_a14db589), and
   facility_element_of_a_cancellation_settlement_ce5be7be: *"A facility fee has been posted when
   facility fee lines stand on the folio for more than nothing."*
3. The adjunct is non-finite and causal — it explains *why* the whole of it is owed (the plan does
   not waive it) — and to reach 232.00 it would have to override its own head noun.

It is worth recording, however, that the baseline's own worked example does not by itself
discriminate between the two readings: it takes *"a property facility fee of 140.00 USD"* on 1 room
over 4 nights, and 140.00 is simultaneously the posted figure and 35.0 × 1 × 4. The exclusion
therefore rests on (1) and (2), not on the example. I record this as a re-checkable judgement rather
than a defect; on the corpus as published the reading is not equally reasonable, so it is not a
second formula the KB offers.

Where the corpus leaves a boundary open it is left open: nothing fixes whether P3 is run before or
after P2, and nothing needs to — neither figure is an input to the other. Recorded as an openness,
not a document defect.

### Counter-proof B — the wrong answer "do only the one thing he asked for"

Closing the stay straight away is excluded by the visible principles plus the records:

   highest night sequence the folio's room lines carry."* occurs **verbatim 6 times**, in exactly the
